full_judgment:
Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule are that Opposite Party No.1, Md. Yousuf Ali filed Miscellaneous Case No.37 of 1992 (subsequently renumbered as 16 of 1995) before the Assistant Judge, Debhata, Satkhira for pre-emption of the case land under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. His case, in a nutshell, was that he was a co-sharer in the case land. The petitioner Md. Ferajtulla Sheikh sold the case land to opposite party Nos.2-3 without any notice to him. He came to learn about the sale, for the first time on 13.9.1992 and thereafter obtained a certified copy of the sale deed and filed the application for pre-emption within time. 

 Mrs. Joya Barttacharjee, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the lower appellate Court without any independent discussion over the issues mechanically dittoed the trial Court’s judgment and thereby committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. She further submits that since the case land had been returned to the vendor by a reconveyance deed executed before filing of the miscellaneous case, it cannot be preempted within the scope of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.
